title: Company-wide policies and processes (access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose
-------
This document centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, contractors, and vendors who interact with Redwood systems or incur company expenses.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood employees, full-time contractors, and approved third-party vendors.
Excluded: external partners under separate master agreements where bespoke policies are documented in the contract.

Primary contacts and ownership
------------------------------
- Policy owner: People Ops (owner_team)
- Security & Compliance: advisory owner for access/data/change policies
- Finance: advisory owner for procurement and expenses
- IT/Platform: operational owner for system access and change implementation

1) Access & permissions
-----------------------
Principles
- Principle of least privilege (PoLP): users and services are granted the minimum access necessary.
- Role-based access control (RBAC): access is granted via predefined roles where possible.
- Time-bounded access: elevated access should be time-limited and audited.

Onboarding and role changes (standard flow)
1. New-hire receives a role definition and onboarding checklist from People Ops.
2. Hiring manager submits an Access Request (Jira form or internal portal) listing required roles/services.
3. IT/Platform approves and provisions access; default access is no privileged permissions.
4. People Ops verifies completion during day-3 onboarding.

Elevated access / temporary privilege
- Requests for elevated access (e.g., admin, production write) must include business justification, duration (max 7 days without re-approval), and owner approval.
- Approvals: manager -> service owner -> security reviewer (for production-impacting access).
- Example: SSH or console access to production clusters requires a two-factor approval and a ticket number for audit linking.

Periodic review and revocation
- Quarterly access review: service owners review members of privileged groups.
- Offboarding: People Ops triggers immediate revocation of access on termination.

Access approval matrix (summary)
| Request type | Approver(s) | Max approved duration | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Standard role assignment | Service owner or IT | Permanent based on role | Assigned via RBAC groups |
| Elevated (admin) | Manager + Service owner + Security | 7 days | Must supply justification |
| Vendor access | Vendor owner + Security + Legal | 30 days (renewal) | Requires signed NDA and approved contract |

Requesting access: checklist
- Business justification
- Least-privilege role selected
- Expected duration
- Test account or audit plan (if production access)

2) Change management
--------------------
Classification
- Standard: low-risk, documented changes that follow an approved runbook (automated deployment, config flag flips).
- Significant: changes with potential customer impact or > 5% capacity change (requires change review board sign-off).
- Emergency: critical fixes needed to mitigate an active incident or outage.

Planned change workflow
1. Create a Change Request (CR) in the change management system including impact assessment, rollback plan, and test plan.
2. Peer review and service owner approval.
3. Schedule change in the maintenance calendar and notify stakeholders (72h notice for Significant changes).
4. Runbook, safety checks, and monitoring playbook attached.
5. Post-change verification and update of runbooks.

Change review board (CRB)
- Meets twice weekly. Members: Engineering leads (infra, platform, runtime), SRE, Security, Product operations, and a Finance representative for capacity/cost-impact reviews.
- Criteria for escalation: cross-service impacts, regulatory scope, customer-facing SLA risk.

Emergency change process
1. During incidents, engineering may execute Emergency Changes only with incident lead and security approval.
2. Post-facto CR required within 48 hours documenting justification, outcome, and follow-up remediation.

3) Data management
------------------
Data classification
- Public: information safe to publish.
- Internal: non-sensitive company data (default).
- Confidential: customer or business data that requires controlled access.
- Restricted: regulated data (PII, financial data subject to regulation) with strongest controls.

Handling rules
- Confidential and Restricted data must be stored only in approved systems (see Appendix: Approved Services).
- Encryption at rest and in transit is mandatory for Confidential and Restricted data.
- Export controls: data leaving the company (download, third-party transfer) requires business owner and security approval.

Retention and deletion
- All datasets must have a documented retention period. Default retention: Internal = 2 years, Confidential = 7 years, Restricted = per contractual/regulatory requirement.
- Data deletion requests processed through the Data Subject Request (DSR) workflow where applicable.

Backups and disaster recovery
- Critical datasets backed up daily with off-site replication.
- Recovery point objectives (RPO) and recovery time objectives (RTO) are defined per dataset in the Data Inventory.

Audit and monitoring
- Access to Confidential and Restricted data is logged. Monthly audit reports are produced for owners.
- Security conducts annual data handling audits and ad-hoc audits for any incident with potential data exposure.

4) Procurement & expenses
-------------------------
Procurement principles
- Approvals based on spend thresholds to balance speed and fiscal control.
- Use preferred vendors and existing master agreements where available.

Spend and approval matrix
| Spend range | Required approvals | Procurement path |
|---:|---|---|
| <= $500 | Manager | Expense report (Concur) |
| $501 - $10,000 | Manager + Finance reviewer | Purchase order (PO) recommended |
| > $10,000 | Manager + Finance manager + Procurement lead | Formal procurement with vendor evaluation |

Purchase workflow (high level)
1. Requestor completes Procurement Request form with justification, cost center, and vendor details.
2. Manager approval -> Finance review for budget availability -> Procurement reviews contract terms (if required).
3. Purchase via PO or card depending on category.
4. Receipt and invoice routed to Finance for payment and GL coding.

Expense policy (employee reimbursements)
- Use company card where practical. For reimbursements, submit receipts in Concur within 30 days.
- Eligible expenses: travel, client meals with pre-approval, event sponsorships per guidelines.
- Ineligible expenses: personal entertainment, non-business upgrades, fines.

Travel booking and approvals (summary)
- All travel requires manager approval in advance. Bookings should use preferred travel vendors listed in the Travel section.
- International travel that involves export-control risk or Restricted data requires Security and Legal pre-clearance.

5) Vendor management
--------------------
Onboarding checklist
1. Complete Vendor Intake form including business justification, contact information, and data access requirements.
2. Security & Legal perform risk classification (low/medium/high). High-risk vendors require a security assessment and contract clauses (DPA, SOC2, liability caps).
3. Procurement executes contract negotiation and signs a Master Services Agreement (MSA) where appropriate.
4. Access provisioning follows the Access & permissions policy and is time-limited.

Vendor monitoring and SLAs
- Maintain an approved vendor inventory with classification and renewal dates.
- For vendors with SLAs affecting customer experience, include monitoring and escalation hooks in the contract.
- Annual vendor review: performance, security posture, and cost-effectiveness.

Offboarding and termination
- Revoke all vendor accounts and keys on contract expiry or termination.
- Retrieve or securely delete vendor-held data per contract requirements.
- Document lessons learned and update the vendor inventory.

6) Travel policy (detailed guidance)
----------------------------------
Booking and class of travel
- Domestic flights: economy/coach. Exceptions (business class) require VP-level approval for flights > 6 hours.
- Hotels: preferred corporate rates recommended; reasonableness standard applies.
- Ground transport: rideshare or rental car as appropriate; rental cars for multi-stop or remote travel.

Per diem and meals
- Per diem follows regional guidelines. Default: $75/day in North America, $100/day for APAC business centers with high local costs.
- Alcohol at client meals may be expensed with manager pre-approval and within reason.

Insurance and emergency support
- Company travel insurance covers approved business travel. People Ops coordinates emergency assistance.

Reimbursement procedure
1. Submit receipts and business purpose in Concur within 30 days.
2. Manager approves -> Finance processes reimbursement within the next payroll cycle.

7) Internal templates and references
----------------------------------
Common templates (available in the Templates library)
- Procurement request form (procurement-request-template.docx)
- Access request form (access-request-jira-template.json)
- Vendor intake checklist (vendor-intake-template.xlsx)
- Expense reimbursement form (expense-reimbursement-template.pdf)
- Standard change request template (change-request-template.md)
- Travel authorization form (travel-request-template.docx)

How to use templates
- Templates are stored in the Company Templates Confluence space and synced to the corporate Google Drive. Use the relevant template and attach completed forms to requests in the ticketing systems.

8) Compliance, audits and exceptions
-----------------------------------
- Exceptions: any deviation from these policies requires a documented exception request and approval from the policy owner and an executive sponsor. Exceptions are timeboxed and reviewed quarterly.
- Audits: Finance, Security, and People Ops run periodic audits. Findings generate remediation plans with owners and due dates.

9) Operating rhythm and review cadence
-------------------------------------
- Annual policy review: People Ops coordinates an annual review with stakeholders (Security, Finance, IT, Legal, Engineering) to update thresholds, approvals, and templates.
- Quarterly spot checks: Ad-hoc reviews of expense reports, access lists, and vendor inventory.

Appendix: quick reference tables and links
-----------------------------------------
Approved services (examples)
- Identity & Access: Okta (SSO), GSuite, internal IAM
- Data storage: S3 (encrypted buckets), Redshift (restricted), internal DB clusters
- Procurement: Concur (expenses), Ariba (POs), Stripe (vendor payments)

Contacts
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Finance: finance@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Security: security@redwood.com

Frequently asked questions
- Q: Who approves vendor access to production?
  A: Service owner + Security + Legal (if data access is required).
- Q: How long do I have to submit receipts?
  A: 30 days; late submissions require manager + Finance approval.

Change log
- 2026-02-15: Initial published baseline (A. Patel).

End of document
